Industry focus

One value chain, many data owners.

Each organization contributes a different part of the product story. A practical TDG or DPP programme begins by identifying which records matter for the agreed product and partner relationship.

Apparel & Textiles

Jhut & Recycling

Sustainable Supply Chain

Fibre / raw materials→Yarn & fabric→Dyeing / finishing→Garment production→Buyer / market→Reuse / recycling

Who the work can serve

Different starting points. A shared data journey.

Garment exporters and factories

Map product specifications, BOMs, purchase orders, production records and evidence. Assign owners and prepare repeatable responses to buyer data requests.

Mills and processors

Connect material and processing information to the relevant customer, product, order or batch. Make provenance, review status and sharing permissions explicit.

Trims, accessories and packaging suppliers

Clarify which data fields and supporting documents are needed for the selected product and how to submit updates without unnecessary duplicate requests.

Brands, buyers and buying houses

Define supplier onboarding, product-data requirements, source quality, access levels and handoffs to a buyer system or DPP platform selected for the programme.

A factory-aware approach

Start with operational records—not assumptions.

Factories and suppliers have different combinations of ERP, PLM, MES, buyer portals, spreadsheets, PDFs and paper records. The engagement should inventory the current sources and identify which data can be reused before adding manual reporting or software.

For an agreed apparel pilot, information may be mapped across style and variant references, material and supplier records, processing stages, purchase orders, batch/lot identifiers, test reports and certificates. These are preparation topics—not a final legal DPP field list.

Jhut and textile-waste information can become a relevant circularity use case where a client has a real collection, handler or recycling workflow. It should complement—not replace—the product identity, supplier governance and evidence work needed for a DPP programme.

Know who has which responsibility

A Bangladesh factory may be an important source of product and production data. Do not assume every upstream factory is automatically the economic operator responsible for placing a product on the EU market; roles depend on the product, commercial arrangement and applicable rules.
